name: Next.js SaaS assurance pack
limitations: This pack measures only the documented static patterns and named runtime evidence requirements.
A clean result does not certify framework security, authorization, tenant isolation, or payment correctness.
Row-level security, cache isolation, webhook replay resistance, and deployed configuration require runtime evidence.

checks.summary: Client-exposed environment prefixes must not carry secret-like values.
checks.safePattern: Read STRIPE_SECRET_KEY only in server code.
checks.verification: Inspect the built client bundle and confirm the secret value is absent.
limitations: Name-based detection cannot identify a secret with a benign variable name.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Detects only recognized public prefixes and secret-like names.

checks.summary: Privileged service clients must not be constructed in a client component.
checks.safePattern: Construct privileged clients in a server-only module or route.
checks.verification: Build the app and inspect client chunks for the privileged credential.
limitations: Aliased constructors or credentials hidden behind helper calls may not match.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Static source match does not inspect the emitted bundle.

checks.summary: Mutation route handlers should show an authorization decision.
checks.insecureExample: export async function POST(req) { return db.user.delete(...) }
checks.safePattern: Resolve and validate the caller session before the mutation.
checks.verification: Exercise the route unauthenticated and as a second user; both must be denied.
limitations: Project-specific auth wrappers and intentionally public routes require review.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Auth may be enforced by middleware or an unrecognized wrapper.

checks.summary: Redirect destinations must not come directly from request input.
checks.safePattern: Map an allowlisted destination key to a local path.
checks.verification: Supply an external URL and confirm the response cannot redirect off-site.
limitations: Data-flow through helper functions may not be detected.

checks.summary: Authenticated and tenant data must not cross cache keys or revalidation boundaries.
checks.insecureExample: Cache a tenant query under one global key.
checks.safePattern: Include authorization scope in the cache key or opt sensitive reads out of shared caching.
checks.verification: Probe the same cached route as two users and two tenants after revalidation.
limitations: Cache isolation cannot be established from source syntax alone.

checks.summary: Service-role clients require an explicit server-only trust boundary.
checks.safePattern: Isolate the service-role client in a server-only admin module with caller checks.
checks.verification: Trace every caller and confirm no untrusted request can select arbitrary rows.
limitations: A privileged client can be valid; this rule identifies a mandatory review point.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Static construction alone cannot prove authorization is missing.

checks.summary: Request-selected rows depend on verified RLS or explicit ownership scope.
checks.safePattern: Use authenticated-user scope and verified RLS policies.
checks.verification: Read the row as a second user and confirm the database denies it.
limitations: Static analysis cannot inspect deployed RLS policies.

assuranceMappings.limitation: A finding may be protected by deployed RLS.

checks.summary: RLS must deny cross-user reads and writes for every exposed table.
checks.insecureExample: An authenticated user can select or update another user's row.
checks.safePattern: Enable RLS and define least-privilege owner or tenant policies.
checks.verification: Run two-user read and mutation probes against the deployed database.
limitations: Local source files do not prove the policies deployed to the target database.

checks.summary: Prisma reads and mutations selected by request ID should include owner or tenant scope.
checks.safePattern: Include userId, ownerId, tenantId, organizationId, or accountId in the query.
checks.verification: Attempt the operation using another user's object ID.
limitations: Authorization enforced before the query may make a finding safe.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Recognizes direct request expressions and common scope fields.

checks.summary: An unfiltered request body must not become Prisma mutation data.
checks.safePattern: Parse an allowlisted input schema and construct mutation data explicitly.
checks.verification: Submit an authorization-sensitive field and confirm it is rejected.
limitations: Aliases and helper-mediated request data may evade direct matching.

checks.summary: Drizzle queries selected by request ID should combine owner or tenant scope.
checks.safePattern: Combine ID and authenticated ownership predicates with and().
checks.verification: Attempt the operation using another user's object ID.
limitations: The current rule recognizes direct request expressions, not arbitrary data flow.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Static syntax cannot prove upstream authorization.

checks.summary: An unfiltered request body must not become a Drizzle update set.
checks.safePattern: Parse an allowlisted input schema and set explicit fields.
checks.verification: Submit an authorization-sensitive field and confirm it is rejected.
limitations: Aliases and helper-mediated request data may evade direct matching.

checks.summary: Destructive migration statements require explicit data-preservation review.
checks.safePattern: Use an expand-migrate-contract sequence with backup and rollback evidence.
checks.verification: Apply the migration to a production-like snapshot and verify preserved data and rollback.
limitations: A matched destructive operation may be intentional but remains release-sensitive.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Detects named destructive SQL statements in recognized migration paths.

checks.summary: Stripe webhook payloads must be verified from the raw body before parsing or acting.
checks.verification: Replay a payload with an invalid signature and confirm rejection before side effects.
limitations: Custom verification wrappers may require a waiver after review.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Path and syntax heuristic does not prove all webhook entry points.

checks.summary: Repeated delivery of one Stripe event must produce at most one business side effect.
checks.insecureExample: Each delivery independently grants credits or fulfills an order.
checks.safePattern: Persist the event ID transactionally before applying an idempotent side effect.
checks.verification: Deliver the same signed event twice concurrently and compare durable outcomes.
limitations: Replay resistance depends on durable state and transaction behavior.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Requires runtime concurrency and durable-state evidence.

checks.summary: Payment amount, price, and product selection must be server-authoritative.
checks.safePattern: Resolve an allowlisted server-side price or product record.
checks.verification: Tamper with the client amount or price ID and confirm the server ignores or rejects it.
limitations: Data flow through intermediate helpers may not be detected.

checks.summary: Request-selected Stripe customer or account IDs require local ownership validation.
checks.safePattern: Load the customer ID from the authenticated user's server-side account record.
checks.verification: Supply another user's customer ID and confirm denial before the Stripe call.
limitations: Upstream ownership checks may make a direct call safe.

assuranceMappings.limitation: Direct request-expression heuristic cannot see all upstream guards.
